newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab family lives uneasily on Hebron firing line.
newsitem.headline: Arab family lives uneasily on Hebron firing line.

text.p: It's a prime piece of real estate with little peace and quiet.
Welcome to the Hebron house of horror, a petrol bomb-scorched apartment building where the Palestinian Abu Zeineh family now has Israeli snipers on the roof and in two empty flats as armed squatters.

The house on Old Well Street has a view to die for. It stands just inside the Israeli-controlled sector of Hebron, overlooking the Palestinian-ruled part of the city and a confrontation line where fighting has raged for days.
"This is the centre of the Palestinian crisis," lamented Safa Abu Zeineh. "On our rooftop," her husband Nihad added sadly.

The couple and their five children, aged between one and five, are caught in the middle of a wave of violence largely touched off by the discovery on Hebron storefronts on Saturday of a poster depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
"My children and I live in a war. We are scared all the time. It is a terrible situation," Safa Abu Zeineh said.
She said five-year-old Zeid had been looking out the window during clashes two months ago and saw a child shot in the eye.
"The situation now is very bad...I am very worried about my kids, what they are going through and what kind of psychological effect it is having on them," Nihad Abu Zeineh said.
The family said soldiers storm into the building to take up positions whenever violence erupts.
"Yesterday, I opened my door and soldiers said: 'What are you doing? Shut the door'," Safa said.

The roof of the three-storey building is strewn with empty boxes of metal-coated rubber bullets used by Israeli marksmen. Black marks from petrol bombs thrown from the street below dot the building's stone facade.
"I am waiting for it to get quiet, so I can do my laundry and hang it on the roof," Nihad said.
Jews were once more welcome in the family home. Nihad pulled out a certificate in Hebrew that includes his grandfather in a list of 20 Arabs who hid Jews during a 1929 massacre in Hebron.

Nihad, a 33-year-old unemployed medic, said he had appealed to the Palestinian Authority for help in renting a home in the PLO-controlled part of the city but was told it could not help him because he lived on the Israeli side.
"No one in the world can solve my problem," he said.
